def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0]); bg=grid[0][0]
    # locate unique compact motif, then use its four arms as a directional stencil
    cells=[(r,c,grid[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c]!=bg]
    # motif is the densest 3x3 neighborhood; its pattern radiates through marker points
    best=None
    for r,c,_ in cells:
      n=sum(1 for rr,cc,v in cells if abs(rr-r)<=2 and abs(cc-c)<=2)
      if best is None or n>best[0]: best=(n,r,c)
    _,cr,cc=best
    # source motif is 3x3 centered approx at (cr,cc); infer colors by nearest input cell at each relative offset
    motif={(r-cr,c-cc):v for r,c,v in cells if abs(r-cr)<=1 and abs(c-cc)<=1}
    out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    # rays extend horizontally/vertically in the motif's occupied offsets; repeat offset color progression
    for r,c,v in cells:
      if v==bg: continue
      if abs(r-cr)<=1 and abs(c-cc)<=1: continue
      dr=r-cr; dc=c-cc
      if dr==0: continue
      step=1 if dr>0 else -1
      # vertical rays use motif's top/bottom row, repeating the three-color motif down to edge
      for rr in range(cr+step, r+step, step):
        off=((rr-cr)%3-1,0)
        color=motif.get(off)
        if color is not None: out[rr][c]=color
    return out
PY
